A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Hydra. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated diagrams and renumbered appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original Hydra experiments on seven benchmarks, together with ablations, robustness tests, faithfulness analyses, and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in the main text and appendices, including Tables 1–9.

M1.justification: The exploration phases, source selection, verification scores, pruning, and answering procedures remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–4 and the prompt templates retain the same substantive content.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same seven benchmarks using the same knowledge sources. The incomplete-KG scenarios and multi-hop and multi-entity coverage are also retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain IO, CoT, SC, text/web RAG, ToG, PoG, CoK, and ToG-2. Changing the category label from KG-centric RAG to KG-based RAG does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Splits, sample sizes, Hits@1 evaluation, backbone models, KG-completeness levels, and implementation settings are retained. Table 1's expanded GPT-3.5-Turbo labels agree with v1's caption and experimental details; they do not establish a model-setting change.

E4.justification: Table 3 narrowly revises the evidence about web-document contribution on CWQ: excluding web documents now produces a 3.2-point drop from the all-source score, versus 13.2 points previously. The ablation conditions and remaining robustness, supplementary analyses, and case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed values, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes CWQ accuracy for 'w/o Web document' from 65 in v1 to 75.0 in v2; the all-source value remains 78.2. No corresponding setting change or explanation is supplied. Other matched numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The reasoning-path definitions, path constraints, scoring equations, and overlap formula are unchanged. Section 3 relabels KGQA/G as KBQA/B to match the existing broader knowledge-source setting, without introducing new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The claims of training-free, structured cross-source reasoning, seven-benchmark superiority, and improved performance with smaller backbones remain unchanged, including the headline comparisons with ToG-2.

C2.justification: The interpretations of source integration, robustness, faithfulness, errors, and efficiency are retained. The limitation concerning absent image/video modalities and the ethical-bias discussion are also unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code access link in the abstract and Appendix C, absent from v1. Implementation parameters, algorithms, and prompts otherwise remain unchanged. The PDFs establish the access pointer, not whether its destination is functional.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations throughout the introduction, related work, and experimental appendix, including adaptive-retrieval, multimodal-QA, and graph-research references. These mainly supplement background statements; substantive positioning against ToG-2, PoG, and other hybrid RAG approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 updates terminology, affiliations, and cross-references, adds acknowledgments, and removes the separate workflow-summary appendix after moving its diagrams into the main text. Most explanatory prose and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The architecture and initialization diagrams move from v1 Appendix B to v2 Figures 2–3 in the main text. Figure 1 and Tables 1–2 are enlarged, the retained diagrams are resized, and a title logo is added. The visual content is largely preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 improves readability through larger figures and tables and places the workflow diagrams alongside the method. The added code-access pointer improves reproducibility documentation. These are limited gains: the scientific evidence is largely unchanged, and the unexplained Table 3 revision does not establish improved empirical reliability.
